title: KV Cache-Aware Routing and P/D Disaggregation on Kubernetes — Yuchen Fama & Ashish Kamra, Red Hat
talk_summary: Red Hat engineers describe LLM-d's KV-cache-aware endpoint routing and prefill/decode disaggregation for agentic inference on Kubernetes, with benchmarks showing large inter-token-latency and throughput gains. The core lesson is that agentic workloads have huge, highly variable contexts and >90% prefix-cache hit rates, so routing requests to pods that already hold the prefix cache is a major latency and cost lever.

takeaways.what_they_do: The router's endpoint picker probes each inference pod for running/waiting requests, KV-cache utilization, and prefix-cache availability, then routes each request to the pod with the lowest load and highest probability of a cache hit.
takeaways.evidence_quote: score each pod on like the running for example running and waiting request and then the KV cache utilization also prefix uh cache availability
takeaways.numbers: Demo: first turn ~3s, cache-hit turn ~1s; agentic workloads show cache hit rates 'well exceeding 90%'

takeaways.technique: Measure cache-hit throughput separately from raw throughput
takeaways.what_they_do: They argue capacity planning and metrics must separate cached-token throughput from total throughput and look at P90 distributions, not averages, because agentic context sizes vary wildly.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we need to measure cats throughput separately. Why? Because on the right, it's really clear that economic stakes is very high
takeaways.numbers: 10x cost difference between cached and non-cached tokens (Anthropic API pricing)

takeaways.technique: Stable-prefix prompt structure for cache reuse
takeaways.what_they_do: They note agents reuse system prompts and tool definitions heavily, yielding very high cache hit rates; keeping the prefix identical across turns is what makes cache hits possible.
takeaways.evidence_quote: agent frequently reuse the uh system prompt and the total definitions we usually see super high cash hit rate

takeaways.technique: Prefill/decode disaggregation (only if you self-host inference)
takeaways.what_they_do: Separate prefill (compute-heavy, bursty) from decode (memory-bandwidth, latency-sensitive) into independently scalable pools, transferring KV cache over a fast fabric (RDMA/RoCE) via NIXL.
takeaways.evidence_quote: colloccating uh both prefill and decode tasks on the same GPU creates something called as phase interference
takeaways.numbers: P99 ITL ~900ms aggregated vs ~100ms PD (~9x better); 2P/1D gave 4x better TTFT and 60% more requests on a 45:1 ISL/OSL agentic set

takeaways.technique: Capacity planning on P90 context distributions
takeaways.what_they_do: They warn against averaging context sizes for capacity planning because agentic context is high-variance; use distributions and P90, and account for sub-agent fan-out complicating scheduling.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we can't just simply take the average and oftentimes we need to look at the distributions and the P90 numbers especially when you do uh capacity planning
